questions.q: Based on the alphabetical order, three of the following four are alike in a certain way and thus form a group. Which is the one that does not belong to that group? (Note: The odd man out is not based on the number of consonants/vowels or their position in the letter cluster.)
questions.solution:
The normal steps are -4 and +2 between consecutive letters. MIL uses -4 and +3, so it is the odd cluster.
**Answer: MIL**

questions.q: Which of the following letter-number clusters will replace the question mark (?) in the given series to make it logically complete? MPL 79 KNJ 87 ILH 95 GJF 103 ?
questions.solution:
All letters move back two places, and the number increases by eight. GJF103 is followed by EHD111.
**Answer: EHD 111**

questions.q: Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/subtracting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.) (9, 17, 7) (6, 12, 5)
questions.solution:
The middle number is first + third + 1. In (4, 9, 4), 4 + 4 + 1 = 9, matching the given sets.
**Answer: (4, 9, 4)**

questions.q: In a certain code language, ‘LITE’ is coded as ‘3492’ and ‘TIME’ is coded as ‘3954’. What is the code for ‘M’ in the given code language?
questions.solution:
I, T and E are common to LITE and TIME, sharing codes 3, 4 and 9. M is the extra letter in TIME and therefore uses the extra code 5.
**Answer: 5**

questions.q: Seven people, B, C, O, P, Q, R and S, are sitting in a straight line, facing north. Q sits second from the left end of the line. Only two people sit between Q and R. C sits immediately to the right of S. O sits immediately to the left of B. Only one person sits between R and S. How many people sit between P and O?
questions.solution:
From left to right the order is P, Q, S, C, R, O, B. Five positions separate P and O, leaving four people between them.
**Answer: Four**

questions.q: If ‘A’ stands for ‘÷’, ‘B’ stands for ‘×’, ‘C’ stands for ‘+’ and ‘D’ stands for ‘−’, then what will come in place of the question mark (?) in the following equation? 19 D 54 A 6 C 4 B 2 = ?
questions.solution:
Replace the codes: 19 - 54/6 + 4 × 2 = 19 - 9 + 8 = 18.
**Answer: 18**

questions.q: Refer to the following number and symbol series and answer the question that follows. All numbers are single-digit numbers only. (Left) $ 8 6 2 @ $ # 1 5 # % * 9 7 5 @ 3 # 1 * 4 $ (Right) If all the symbols are dropped from the series, which of the following will be sixth from the right?
questions.solution:
Removing symbols gives 8, 6, 2, 1, 5, 9, 7, 5, 3, 1, 4. The sixth number from the right is 9.
**Answer: 9**

questions.q: A is the wife of D. D has a daughter named X and a son named M. M is married to Y. How is Y related to A?
questions.solution:
M is A’s son and Y is M’s wife. Therefore Y is A’s daughter-in-law, described as her son’s wife.
**Answer: Son's wife**

questions.q: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusion(s) logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All gorillas are monkeys. Some monkeys are baboons. All baboons are chimpanzees. Conclusions: (I) All chimpanzees are monkeys. (II) Some chimpanzees are gorillas.
questions.solution:
Some monkeys are baboons and therefore chimpanzees, but they need not be gorillas. Also chimpanzees can extend outside the monkey group. Neither proposed conclusion follows.
**Answer: Neither conclusion (I) nor (II) follows.**

questions.q: What should come in place of ‘?’ in the given series? 35 37 40 45 52 ?
questions.solution:
The differences are successive primes 2, 3, 5 and 7. Add the next prime, 11, to 52 to get 63.
**Answer: 63**

questions.q: Which of the following letter-clusters should replace # and % so that the pattern and relationship followed between the letter-cluster pair on the left side of :: is the same as that on the right side of :: ? # : KQM :: OUQ : %
questions.solution:
Each letter moves one place backwards. LRN becomes KQM, while OUQ becomes NTP.
**Answer: # = LRN , % = NTP**

questions.q: Which of the following letter-number clusters will replace the question mark “?” in the given series to make it logically complete? AIW 8, YGU 14, WES 20, UCQ 26, ?
questions.solution:
Every letter moves two places backwards and the number rises by six. After UCQ26 comes SAO32.
**Answer: SAO 32**

questions.q: In a certain code language, ‘NICE’ is coded as ‘8246’ and ‘COST’ is coded as ‘3851’. What is the code for 'C’ in the given code language?
questions.solution:
C is the only letter common to NICE and COST. The only shared code digit is 8, so C is coded 8.
**Answer: 8**

questions.q: Select the triad which follows the same pattern as that followed by the two pairs given below. Both pairs follow the same pattern. CLUB-CUBL-ULCB HANG-HNGA-NAHG
questions.solution:
The second cluster uses positions 1, 3, 4, 2; the third uses 3, 2, 1, 4. MASK therefore gives MSKA and SAMK.
**Answer: MASK-MSKA-SAMK**

questions.q: Golu starts from Point A and drives 53 km towards West. He then takes a left turn, drives 50 km, turns left and drives 54 km. He then takes a left turn and drives 60 km. He takes a final left turn, drives 1 km and stops at Point P. How far (shortest distance) and towards which direction should he drive in order to reach Point A again? (All turns are 90-degree turns only, unless specified.)
questions.solution:
West–east movement cancels: -53 + 54 - 1 = 0. Vertical movement leaves him 10 km north of A. He must return 10 km south.
**Answer: 10 km to the South**

questions.q: What will come in place of ‘?’ in the following equation, if ‘+’ and ‘-‘ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 95 ÷ 5 + 378 × 3 - 161 = ?
questions.solution:
After swapping signs, the expression is 95 × 5 - 378/3 + 161 = 475 - 126 + 161 = 510.
**Answer: 510**

questions.q: Select the pair which follows the same pattern as that followed by the two set of pairs given below. Both pairs follow the same pattern. DRU : BWS ZBQ : XGO
questions.solution:
Apply shifts -2, +5 and -2 to the three letter positions. VLM becomes TQK, as required.
**Answer: VLM : TQK**

questions.q: Each of P, Q, R, S, T, U and V has an exam on a different day of a week starting from Monday and ending on Sunday of the same week. V has an exam on Thursday. T has an exam on one of the days after P and on one of the days before U. Q has an exam on one of the days after R but on one of the days before S. R has an exam on one of the days after V. Who has an exam on Sunday?
questions.solution:
R, Q and S must occur in that order after Thursday. They therefore occupy Friday, Saturday and Sunday. S has the Sunday exam.
**Answer: S**

questions.q: Below are given two sets of numbers. In each set of numbers, a certain mathematical operation on the first number results in the second number. Similarly, certain mathematical operations on the second number result in the third number and so on. Which of the given options follows the same set of operations as in question? (NOTE – A two/three-digit number cannot be broken into individual digits for operations, e.g., if 37 is followed by 10, the operation cannot be 3+7 as a two-digit number cannot be broken into individual digits.) 12 – 26 – 46 – 70; 20 – 34 – 54 – 78
questions.solution:
The operations are +14, +20 and +24. Only 25 → 39 → 59 → 83 follows all three.
**Answer: 25 – 39 – 59 – 83**

questions.q: A, B, C, D, E and F live on six different floors of the same building. The lowermost floor in the building is numbered 1, the floor above it is numbered 2 and so on, till the topmost floor, which is numbered 6. The product of the floors on which D and B live is 15. A lives immediately above F. The sum of the floors on which C and B live is 7. What is the sum of the floors on which B and F live?
questions.solution:
B must be on floor 3 and D on 5; reversing these would block the adjacent F–A pair. C is then on 4, leaving F on 1 and A on 2. B + F = 4.
**Answer: 4**

questions.q: Below are given two sets of numbers. In each set of numbers, a certain mathematical operation on the first number results in the second number. Similarly, a certain mathematical operation on the second number results in the third number and so on. Which of the given options follows the same set of operations as in the question? (NOTE – A two/three-digit number cannot be broken into individual digits for operations. E.g. if 37 is followed by 10, the operation cannot be 3+7 as a two-digit number cannot be broken into individual digits.) 5 – 20 – 60 – 120 8 – 32 – 96 – 192
questions.solution:
Multiply successively by 4, 3 and 2. The matching chain is 10 → 40 → 120 → 240.
**Answer: 10 – 40 – 120 – 240**

questions.q: Refer to the following letter, number, symbol series and answer the question. (Left) 5 C £ T R 6 B $ D © 9 6 * 9 # Z 7 2 R $ O K (Right) If all the symbols are dropped from the series, which of the following will be fourth from the left?
questions.solution:
After dropping symbols, the sequence begins 5, C, T, R, 6, B. The fourth item from the left is R.
**Answer: R**

questions.q: Based on the English alphabetical order, three of the following four letter-cluster pairs are alike in a certain way and thus form a group. Which letter-cluster pair DOES NOT belong to that group? (Note: The odd one out is not based on the number of consonants/vowels or their position in the letter-cluster.)
questions.solution:
Three pairs move both letters ahead by three. BD → FH moves both ahead by four, so it is the odd pair.
**Answer: BD–FH**

questions.q: Refer to the following number and symbol series and answer the question that follows. Counting to be done from left to right only. All numbers are single-digit numbers only. (Left) % 1 7 3 < $ 3 7 4 ^ < & # 5 < 3 ^ % > \ & (Right) How many such symbols are there, each of which is immediately preceded by a number and also immediately followed by a number?
questions.solution:
Only the < symbol between 5 and 3 has a number immediately on each side. Hence one symbol qualifies.
**Answer: One**

questions.q: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. You have to take the given statements to be true even if they seem to be at variance from commonly known facts. You have to decide which conclusion/s logically follow/s from the given statements. Statements: All hands are legs. Some hands are ears. Some ears are arms. Conclusions: (I) Some legs are ears. (II) Some hands are arms.
options: Both conclusions I and II follow.
Neither conclusion I nor II follows.
questions.solution:
Some hands are ears, and all hands are legs, so some legs are ears. The ears that are arms need not be hands. Only conclusion I follows.
**Answer: Only conclusion I follows.**

questions.q: Seven people F, G, H, I, U, V, and W are sitting around a circular table facing the centre of the table. G sits third to the right of U. Only three people sit between F and H when counted from the right of H. G sits to the immediate right of H. V sits to the immediate right of W. Who sits second to the right of I?
questions.solution:
Place G immediately right of H and three right of U, then place F four right of H. The W–V pair occupies the remaining adjacent gap. G is second to I’s right.
**Answer: G**

questions.q: In a certain code language, A@ B means ‘A is the son of B’ A % B means ‘A is the brother of B’ A + B means ‘A is the wife of B’ A & B means ‘ A is the father of B’ Based on the above, how is T related to K if ‘T@S%G+H&K’?
questions.solution:
G is H’s wife and K’s mother. S is G’s brother, and T is S’s son. Therefore T is the son of K’s maternal uncle.
**Answer: Mother's brother's son**

questions.q: In this question, a question is followed by two statements numbered (I) and (II). You have to decide whether the data provided in the statements are sufficient to answer the question. Read both the statements and decide the appropriate answer. Q. Harsh, Ketan, Mayank, Rohit, and Sidharth, each have different height. Who is the shortest? (I) Mayank is taller than Harsh but shorter than Ketan. (II) Rohit is taller than Harsh but shorter than Mayank.
options: Data in Statement II alone is sufficient to answer the question while data in Statement I is not
Both statements I and II together are NOT sufficient to answer the question
Data in Statement I alone is sufficient to answer the question while data in Statement II is not
Both statements I and II together (and not statement I alone or statement II alone) are sufficient to answer the question
questions.solution:
Both statements leave Sidharth’s height unconstrained. He may be shorter than Harsh or taller, so combining the statements still cannot identify the shortest person.
**Answer: Both statements I and II together are NOT sufficient to answer the question**

questions.q: Each of seven people, E, F, G, H, J, K and L, has an exam on a different day of a week, starting from Monday and ending on Sunday of the same week. Only three people have exams between L and J. Only three people have exams between H and K. E has exam on some day before J and on some day after F. Only G has exam before K. How many people have exams before L?
questions.solution:
G is on Monday and K on Tuesday, forcing H onto Saturday. The F–E–J order and the L–J gap place L on Wednesday. Two people have exams before L.
**Answer: Two**

questions.q: What should come in place of ‘?’ in the given series? 23 26 32 41 53 ?
questions.solution:
Differences are 3, 6, 9 and 12, increasing by three. Add 15 next: 53 + 15 = 68.
**Answer: 68**
